title: Contingencies and subsequent events — Lindqvist Mfg.
instructions: Lindqvist Mfg.'s December 31, Year 1 statements will be issued March 15, Year 2. Determine the treatment of each matter and compute the year-end liabilities.

exhibits.title: Matters
exhibits.content:
A. A customer lawsuit: counsel says loss is probable, estimated at **$200,000–$500,000**, with **$300,000** the best estimate.
B. A $1,000,000 patent claim: counsel says an unfavorable outcome is reasonably possible.
C. Warranties: Year 1 sales of **$2,000,000** carry a 1-year assurance warranty; expected claims are **2%** of sales; **$15,000** of claims were paid in Year 1.
D. A November Year 1 forklift accident: at year-end counsel said loss was probable but couldn't estimate it. On February 10, Year 2, the case settled for **$120,000**.
E. On February 20, Year 2, a fire destroyed a warehouse (uninsured loss **$700,000**).
F. The company self-insures its delivery fleet against collision; no accidents occurred in Year 1.

parts.prompt: Select the treatment of each matter in the Year 1 statements.

rows.label: A. Customer lawsuit
rows.explanation: Probable and estimable: accrue the best estimate.

rows.label: B. Patent claim
rows.explanation: Reasonably possible losses are disclosed, not accrued.

rows.label: C. Warranties
rows.explanation: Assurance warranty costs are accrued as sales occur.

rows.label: D. Forklift accident
rows.explanation: The settlement gives evidence about a condition at year-end (recognized subsequent event).

rows.label: E. Warehouse fire
rows.explanation: A condition arising after year-end is a nonrecognized event; disclose if material.

rows.label: F. Self-insurance
rows.explanation: No loss has occurred; future losses aren't accrued.

rows.label: Total accrued litigation liabilities (A and D)
